text: Simple historical rules provide a demanding benchmark for forecasts of peak net-position limits.

The clearest repeated score gains arise for hourly FX positions with a long training history and a short horizon, where quantile regression improves on a historical headroom rule with the same history in both retrospective periods.
The later-period gain also survives the evaluated coverage correction, while the regression breaches more often before correction.
Against the original shorter-history rolling rule, its gain changes sign across the two periods.

Other FX configurations show smaller score gains or losses and adverse breach frequencies, so the evidence supports a narrow comparative advantage rather than a universal claim about conditional models.

For weekly aggregate position categories, historical rules win most of the evaluated comparisons even after heavier regularization, and the earlier-period selection exercise preserves important failures.
Peak-limit models should therefore be evaluated jointly on forecast accuracy, breach frequency and stability across reference rules, periods and related series.
